# Petri Nets as a Universal Abstraction

> A Practitioner's Guide to Modeling with pflow — a technical book arguing
> that Petri nets (places, transitions, arcs, tokens) are one formalism for
> state machines, workflows, resource flows, games, chemical kinetics, ZK
> circuits, and token standards. Every chapter pairs the math with working
> models from the pflow ecosystem: the browser editor (pflow.xyz), the Go
> library (go-pflow), and the code generator / MCP server (pilot.pflow.xyz).
> Models are JSON-LD (`@context: https://pflow.xyz/schema`); the same model
> runs as a discrete net, as a mass-action ODE system, and as a verified
> application.

Read it linearly for the argument, or jump to Part II for worked examples
and Part IV for the tooling. The full text in one file is at
[llms-full.txt](https://book.pflow.xyz/llms-full.txt).

## Front matter

- [Preface](https://book.pflow.xyz/preface.html): why a 1962 formalism
  deserves working programmers' attention, who the book is for, how it is
  organized

## Part I: Foundations

- [Why Petri Nets?](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch01-why-petri-nets.html): what
  breaks in flowcharts, state machines and ad-hoc models, and what a
  bipartite graph with tokens fixes (concurrency, conservation, analysis)
- [The Mathematics of Flow](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch02-mathematics-of-flow.html):
  the formal 5-tuple, firing rules, incidence matrix, state equation,
  P- and T-invariants, reachability
- [From Discrete to Continuous](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch03-discrete-to-continuous.html):
  relaxing integer tokens to concentrations — mass-action kinetics, the ODE
  system a net induces, and why adaptive Runge-Kutta (Tsit5) is the default
- [The Token Language](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch04-token-language.html): the
  four-term pflow DSL for guards, roles, typed state, invariants and
  categorical net types (ResourceNet, GameNet, WorkflowNet, ...)

## Part II: Applications

- [Resource Modeling — The Coffee Shop](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch05-resource-modeling.html):
  inventory, recipes and throughput as token flow; finding bottlenecks and
  stock-outs by simulation
- [Game Mechanics — Tic-Tac-Toe](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch06-game-mechanics.html):
  board, turns and win conditions as a GameNet; strategic value emerging from
  topology alone via ODE move evaluation
- [Constraint Satisfaction — Sudoku](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch07-constraint-satisfaction.html):
  constraints as token conservation, continuous relaxation as a move-ranking
  heuristic
- [Optimization — The Knapsack Problem](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch08-optimization.html):
  approximate solutions to an NP-hard problem with mass-action dynamics
- [Biochemistry — Enzyme Kinetics](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch09-enzyme-kinetics.html):
  the formalism's home turf — recovering Michaelis-Menten from a net
- [Complex State Machines — Texas Hold'em](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch10-complex-state-machines.html):
  multi-player, multi-phase systems with roles and guards

## Part III: Advanced Topics

- [Process Mining](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch11-process-mining.html):
  discovering nets from event logs, conformance checking, prediction
- [Zero-Knowledge Proofs](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch12-zero-knowledge-proofs.html):
  proving a transition fired validly without revealing the marking (gnark,
  MiMC, hand-built circuits)
- [Topology-Driven Verification](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch13-topology-driven-verification.html):
  generating ZK circuits automatically from net topology with petrigen
- [On-Chain ZK Verification](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch14-on-chain-verification.html):
  guards and invariants as arithmetic constraints, Merkle-committed state,
  Solidity verifiers
- [Exponential Weights and Scoring Systems](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch15-exponential-weights.html):
  power-of-2 arc weights to encode scoring and ranking in net structure
- [Declarative Infrastructure](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch16-declarative-infrastructure.html):
  JSON-LD, semantic vocabularies, and content addressing (CIDs) that make
  nets self-describing and composable across tools

## Part IV: Building with pflow

- [The Visual Editor — pflow.xyz](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch17-visual-editor.html):
  designing nets interactively, how the drawing maps to the formalism,
  export/import
- [Code Generation — From Model to Application](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch18-code-generation.html):
  petri-pilot — from a JSON model to a Go backend, event store and JS
  frontend that survive regeneration
- [The go-pflow Library](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch19-go-pflow-library.html):
  package layout, builder API, solver configuration, state machines and
  workflows
- [Dual Implementation and Verification](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch20-dual-implementation.html):
  Go/JS parity, event sourcing, and state roots as proof of an unambiguous
  specification

## Epilogue

- [What the Abstraction Sits On](https://book.pflow.xyz/ch21-epilogue.html):
  the layered architecture the book actually built, the six applications
  seen as net types, and open problems

## Appendices

- [Solver Parameter Reference](https://book.pflow.xyz/appendix-a-solver-reference.html):
  Tsit5 and other methods, tolerances, presets in go-pflow's `solver`
- [Token Language Grammar](https://book.pflow.xyz/appendix-b-token-grammar.html):
  S-expression DSL lexer and grammar
- [JSON Schema Reference](https://book.pflow.xyz/appendix-c-json-schema.html):
  the petri-pilot model format — places, transitions, arcs, roles, views,
  event sourcing
- [Glossary](https://book.pflow.xyz/appendix-d-glossary.html): definitions
  from arc to T-invariant
- [Categorical Foundations](https://book.pflow.xyz/appendix-e-categorical-foundations.html):
  symmetric monoidal categories and the formal framework behind the net types

  ([llms.txt](https://pflow.xyz/llms.txt))
- [pilot.pflow.xyz](https://pilot.pflow.xyz): code generation and the

- [blog.stackdump.com](https://blog.stackdump.com): essays the book grew out of
- [Source](https://github.com/pflow-xyz/book-pflow-xyz): markdown chapters,
